UK Ferry Crossings for Motorcycle Tourers

Britain's islands are some of its greatest riding destinations, and ferries are the gateway. From the short CalMac hops to the Scottish islands to the longer crossings to the Channel Islands and Isle of Man, understanding the UK's ferry network opens up touring possibilities that most riders never explore.

The Major Ferry Operators

  • CalMac (Caledonian MacBrayne): Scottish west coast and islands. 30+ routes connecting the mainland to Skye, Mull, Arran, Lewis, Harris, Islay, and more.
  • NorthLink Ferries: Mainland Scotland to Orkney and Shetland. Overnight crossings from Aberdeen or Scrabster.
  • Condor Ferries: Poole/Portsmouth to Channel Islands (Guernsey and Jersey).
  • Isle of Man Steam Packet: Heysham, Liverpool, Dublin, and Belfast to Douglas, Isle of Man.
  • Western Ferries / Argyll Ferries: Short crossings on the Clyde (Gourock to Dunoon).
  • Stena Line / Irish Ferries: Great Britain to Ireland crossings.

Booking Strategy

The right booking approach depends on the route and season:

  • Peak season (June-August): Book 4-8 weeks in advance for popular routes. CalMac to Mull, Condor to Guernsey, and Steam Packet during TT week all sell out.
  • Shoulder season (April-May, September-October): Book 1-2 weeks in advance. More availability, lower prices.
  • Off-season (November-March): Reduced timetables but usually no booking issues. Some routes don't operate in winter.
  • Multi-ferry deals: CalMac Hopscotch tickets and island-hopping passes save money on multi-crossing itineraries.

What Happens at the Terminal

Ferry boarding procedures for motorcycles follow a general pattern across all UK operators:

  • Arrive at the time specified by the operator (typically 30-90 minutes before sailing)
  • Check in at the vehicle lane — show your booking reference and driving licence
  • Wait in the motorcycle queue (usually separate from cars)
  • Board when directed — follow crew instructions for positioning on the car deck
  • Secure your bike (side stand + gear, sometimes crew provide chocks/straps)
  • Take valuables and essentials upstairs — the car deck is sealed during crossing
  • On arrival, return to your bike when the car deck opens and ride off
Motorcycles often board first and disembark last (or vice versa). Don't be frustrated — it's about positioning on the deck. Use the time to enjoy the views from the passenger deck. Ferry crossings are part of the adventure, not just transport.

Tips for Smooth Crossings

  • Put your bike in first gear on deck to prevent rolling
  • Turn off the fuel tap if your bike has one
  • Apply a disc lock for extra security
  • If the sea is rough, check that your bike's position is secure before heading upstairs
  • Carry waterproofs in a day bag — deck conditions can be wet and cold
  • Take motion sickness tablets if you're susceptible — the Irish Sea in particular can be rough

Cost-Saving Tips

  • Motorcycle fares are typically 40-60% of car fares
  • Midweek crossings are cheaper than weekends
  • Off-peak sailings (early morning, late evening) cost less
  • Return bookings are usually cheaper than two singles
  • CalMac's Road Equivalent Tariff (RET) scheme keeps island ferry fares affordable

Combining Ferries into Epic Tours

Some of the best UK motorcycle tours use multiple ferries:

  • The Island Hopper: Mainland → Arran → Mull → Skye → Harris → Lewis → mainland
  • The Crown Dependencies: Poole → Guernsey → Jersey → return, then Heysham → Isle of Man
  • The Northern Isles: Scrabster → Orkney → Shetland → Aberdeen

Ferries add a unique dimension to motorcycle touring. The anticipation as the island appears through the mist, the camaraderie with other riders on deck, and the thrill of riding onto unfamiliar island roads — it's all part of what makes British touring special. faq.q: Do I need to book a motorcycle onto a UK ferry?
faq.a: For popular routes in peak season, June to August, yes: book as early as you can because bike spaces are limited and crossings sell out. In the shoulder seasons of April-May and September-October you have more flexibility, and off-season from November to March you can often turn up and go. Always check timetables, as sailings reduce in winter.

faq.q: How is a motorcycle secured on a ferry?
faq.a: Bikes are usually parked first and secured against the vessel's movement. Some ferries provide straps and crew assistance, but provision varies, so carry your own ratchet straps and soft loops to be safe. Leave the bike in gear with the side stand down, and let the crew guide you on tie-down points before you head up to the passenger deck.

faq.q: What happens at the ferry terminal?
faq.a: Arrive early, check in and join the motorcycle lane. Bikes are typically loaded first and disembark first, which is a real perk. Follow marshals onto the car deck, park where directed, secure the bike, then go up to the lounge for the crossing. Keep your helmet and valuables with you rather than leaving them on the bike.

faq.q: How can I save money on ferry crossings?
faq.a: Motorcycles are charged far less than cars on most routes, and booking early secures the cheapest fares. Look for multi-ferry or island-hopping deals such as CalMac's Hopscotch tickets, travel off-peak where you can, and combine crossings into a single planned route rather than booking each one separately at short notice.
